frontier.hypothesis: With the moved_once channel class-killed (K35), the ONLY remaining loop.c:1631 route is H17's no-carrier window - insn_count in [120,122] with zero emitted bytes - and the only measured free insn_count channel is loop-carried arithmetic deleted by biv elimination (s6), which in every spelling found so far is semantically inert padding.
frontier.mechanism: count_loop_regs_set counts RTL insns in the loop before strength reduction; s6 measured that balanced loop-carried pairs survive cse1, are counted, and are then deleted inside loop_optimize for zero bytes. K21 says only CONSTANT-step bivs get folded away, and K36 now adds that a natural extra index is count-neutral because it displaces the giv multiply it replaces.
frontier.next_probe: Ask whether any SEMANTICALLY REAL loop-carried value this function could plausibly have computed is a constant-step biv: the data at &D_80106A58 is read, not accumulated, and the tail (func_8001CD68 through gpu_DisableDisplay) consumes no per-entry total, so the honest answer is probably no. Settle it by enumerating what a post-loop consumer would have to look like in the target's 23-instruction tail (8003C844..8003C89C) - if no tail instruction can consume an accumulator, the free-insn_count channel is admissible-form-empty and the whole loop.c:1631 axis is closed for ordinary C.

frontier.hypothesis: The last unmeasured admission trigger for the 0x91A2B3C5 movable is count_loop_regs_set's two-basic-block rule (loop.c:3036-3040: n_times_set[regno] > 0 with last_set[regno] == 0 sets may_not_move), which needs ONE pseudo set in two different basic blocks inside the loop - distinct from K23's two-BB experiment, where combine_movables MATCHED two distinct pseudos and raised savings to 2 instead.
frontier.mechanism: may_not_move keeps an insn out of the movable list entirely, which is exactly the target's arrangement (magic in-loop as a split lui/ori pair) and costs nothing on the desirability arithmetic. The open question is purely whether cse1 can leave the magic constant in ONE pseudo that is SET (not merely used) in two basic blocks of the loop.
frontier.next_probe: Build a two-arm loop body where the /1800 division appears in both arms, then read the .cse and .loop dumps rather than the score: check whether the magic appears as one regno with n_times_set 2 (may_not_move fires, no movable printed) or as two regnos joined by combine_movables (K23's outcome). If it is always the latter, the admission axis is closed with a source-level predicate rather than another spelling census.

frontier.hypothesis: pb_array_subscript.c is a byte-equivalent second chassis for this function (15 / 105), so any future permuter or solver campaign has two independent seeds whose RTL converges after cse1.
frontier.mechanism: cse1 folds the array-subscript address arithmetic into the same givs the index-derived-pointer spelling produces, so the two bodies emit identical instructions while presenting different pre-cse RTL to a permuter's mutations.
frontier.next_probe: If a permuter campaign is ever re-run (s4 ran 66,016 iterations on the pointer spelling with zero finds), seed it from tmp/grind/func_8003C714/s12/pb_array_subscript.c instead, so the mutation neighbourhood differs from the exhausted one.
